description: Bodø kommune inviterer til åpen anbudskonkurranse for levering av bedriftshelsetjenester (BHT). Anskaffelsen omfatter lovpålagte og øvrige bedriftshelsetjenester, herunder bistand innen systematisk HMS-arbeid, sykefraværsoppfølging, arbeidsmiljøkartlegging, helseundersøkelser, kurs og rådgivning. Leverandøren skal tilby en tverrfaglig bedriftshelsetjeneste med tilgang til relevante fagressurser og en digital løsning for bestilling, rapportering og statistikk. Det skal inngås rammeavtale med én leverandør for Bodø kommune. Avtalen har en varighet på 4 år med opsjon på ytterligere 2 år.

title: MESO QuickPlex SQ Plate Reader
description: FAR 6.302-1 � Only One Responsible Source Solicitation Number 75N98026Q01214 Title MESO QuickPlex SQ Plate Reader Description of Requirement The National Institutes of Health intends to award a contract to Meso Scale Discovery on a sole-source basis pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, for the acquisition of a MESO QuickPlex� SQ 120MM. The MESO QuickPlex� SQ 120MM Pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, the Government intends to solicit and award a Purchase Order on a sole-source basis because the Government's minimum technical requirements can only be satisfied by the Meso Scale Discovery. The MESO� SECTOR S 600MM, MESO QuickPlex� SQ 120MM, and MESO QuickPlex Q 60MM laboratory analytical instruments are manufactured and sold solely by Meso Scale Discovery (MSD), a division of Meso Scale Diagnostics, LLC. of Rockville, MD. The imagers are compatible only with microwell plates and immunoassay kits sold by MSD and vice versa. MSD utilizes electrochemiluminescence to detect binding events on patterned arrays. There are no other technologies that enable multiplexed measurement using electrochemiluminescence for detection. And there are no other suppliers that provide an electrochemiluminescence detection system that is not reliant on beads or flow cells. The MSD� assay platform is unique in its method for detection as outlined below: � Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) Detection � MSD�s ECL detection utilizes proprietary SULFO-TAG� labels that emit light upon electrochemical stimulation initiated at the electrode surfaces of MULTI-ARRAY� and MULTI-SPOT� microplates through biomolecular interactions between the analyte and labeled reporter at the surface. � Sample Throughput � The SECTOR� S 600MM instrument can read plates in 1 to 1.5 minutes regardless of the multiplexing level. As an illustrative example, the S 600MM instrument can read approximately 50 96-well, 10-spot plates (measuring 10 analytes per each well) per hour resulting in 48,000 measurement per hour. � Non-fluidic, high-reliability instruments � All assay processing and readout steps take place in MSD�s disposable plate-based format. No sample is transferred from the plate to the instrument and hence there are no complicated fluidics that may be prone to clogging and other failures. MSD�s instrumentation has been highly praised by customers for exceptional reliability. The HBGS requires a sensitive, high-throughput analytical platform to support biochemical profiling, multiplex biomarker measurement, and experimental validation relevant to rare biochemical diseases. This activity is directly tied to the Clinical Research activities in the Human Biochemical and Genetics Section (HBGS), which conducts active, protocol?driven patient?based investigations, consistent with NIH definitions of clinical research. The MESO QuickPlex SQ 120MM provides the capabilities necessary for these applications through MSD�s proprietary electrochemiluminescence (ECL) technology, which is only available from Meso Scale Discovery and not offered by any other vendor. The instrument enables rapid multiplex analysis, reading up to 50 plates per hour with high sensitivity and reliability, which is critical for processing diverse patient-derived samples and supporting both research and diagnostics in the Section. The continuation of this project will continue to simulate a clinical trial with our pulmonary fibrosis patients. Accordingly, the Government intends to award a sole-source contract to Meso Scale Discovery, Inc. pursuant to FAR 6.302-1. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required supplies and meet all specified technical and operational requirements. The Government will consider all timely capability statements received and determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to davisroshonna@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 24, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01214 in the subject line of the response.

Solicitation Response Extension The closing date and time for receipt of proposals/quotes is hereby extended from 17 September 2026 to 24 September 2026 to allow the offeror sufficient time to incorporate these updated requirements. 2. The Government reserves the right to request data considered other than certified cost or pricing data from the Contractor to determine the proposed price to be fair and reasonable." 3. As referenced in the above paragraph, Instructions to Offerors, the Government reserves the right to request data considered other than certified cost or pricing data from the Contractor to determine the proposed price to be fair and reasonable. The Government will evaluate and analyze all requested data (if required ) in order to make this determination." All updates and additions withing the soliciaiton are highlighted in yellow for ease of reference. See attached document (AMENDMENT 0001 - COMBO-SOLICITATION FA561327Q0001) No other changes have been made. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- SOLICITATON NOTICE: The 700th Contracting Squadron (700 CONS) intends to award a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) purchase order on a sole source basis to Croner Group Limited (Cage Code: U1AA3); (Unique Entity ID: YL5XL93NM3Y8). This intended contract will cover services in support of the FY27 United Kingdom Wage and Benefit Study Re-Acquisition. The anticipated award date is 30 November 2026. This requirement is to be awarded as a multiple-year follow-on contract inclusive of one (1) 12-month base period with four (4) 12-month option periods in accordance with (IAW) Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 52.217-9. This requirement also includes the Option to Extend Services not to exceed (NTE) 6-months IAW RFO 52.217-8. This intended contract follows the guidance stated in the Department of Defense Manual (DoDM) 1416.08 which mandates compensation for local national personnel supporting U.S. Forces components in the United Kingdom to be based on salary and benefit data analysis. Consistency in the methodology and data source used for these studies is necessary to maintain year-to-year comparability and ensure changes in salary and benefits can be accurately measured. Croner Group Limited is the incumbent contractor under Contract No. FA561322P0008 and currently provides the salary and benefit data used to support this requirement. Croner utilizes established internal systems, methodologies, and historical data to provide consistent employment, wage, and benefit information to the Government. The current contract expires on 31 December 2026, and this follow-on acquisition is intended to ensure continuity of these services. In accordance with RFO 6.103-1, Croner Group Limited is the only responsible source capable of satisfying the Government�s requirement without substantial duplication of cost or unacceptable delays. Award to another source would require the Government and a new contractor to establish a new methodology and data baseline for the wage and benefit studies. This would disrupt year-to-year comparability with historical data and require additional time and resources to establish replacement processes. Additionally, transitioning to another source would create a risk of incompatibility between historical and newly collected salary and benefit data, which could negatively affect the Government�s ability to consistently evaluate changes in compensation. Croner�s established processes and historical data provide the continuity necessary to support the Government�s compensation analysis. Accordingly, the Government intends to solicit and award to Croner Group Limited as the only responsible source capable of meeting this requirement. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes. However interested parties may submit a capability statement upon the referenced deadline within the attached solicitation (FA561327Q0001) demonstrating their ability to perform the requirement described herein. Upon receipt of any such notifications, the Contracting Officer will determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement or proceed with sole source action. Responses received will be reviewed, however; a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no responses are received, the 700 CONS will proceed with the sole source award to Croner Group Limited. See attached solicitation (COMBO-SOLICITATION FA561327Q0001)

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: Whole genome sequencing for investigation of age-related chronic disease in HANDLS participants
description: Investigators in the Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span (HANDLS) study require whole genome sequencing (WGS) processing to expand our current research examining whether genetic variants contribute to age-related chronic diseases. Samples from HANDLS participants have been collected over 20 years and many are over 10 years old. A contract is required because the Government does not have available facilities or resources to perform this work consistent with other WGS performed on other HANDLS samples. The objective of this work is expanding our current research to examine health differences associated with age-related chronic diseases through whole genome sequencing to investigate the contributions of genomics to the burden of disease incidence, prevalence, morbidity, and mortality in populations within the United States. The long-term goal is to create a consistent dataset of whole genome sequencing to complement the longitudinal HANDLS behavior and health data. The contractor will deliver plates to the Government sufficient to run 600 samples, some of which have been stored for ten or more years. The contractor will perform whole genome sequencing, and specifically shall: Sequence libraries on the NovaSeq X-Plus platform with 25B-300 flow cells using 150 bp paired end runs and NovaSeq workflow-series 10B sequencing run confirm genomic DNA quantity and quality by performing DNA concentration measurements and volume checks Re-attempt sequencing in the case that DNA quality and quantity is sufficient, but sample fails sequencing-based quality control Examine agarose gels on all samples as an industry-standard method for screening DNA marker quality prepare PCR-free sequence libraries for all samples Sequence the libraries at a minimum of 30x coverage with 2�150 base pair runs Perform primary and secondary analysis of the sequencing data including but not limited to read alignment, variant calling, and quality control analyses Quality control checks will include confirming sex, identifying unexpected duplicates and relatedness, confirming relatedness, providing sample performance information and sample identity confirmation against the sequencing data, in addition to confirming coverage, contamination, mapped reads, and other general quality metrics. Alignment and variant calling will be performed with the DRAGEN Germline pipeline. After quality is confirmed, joint variant calling should be performed producing a multi-sample VCF file. Provide written summaries and documentation of the methods used to perform the whole genome sequencing pipeline Supply the whole genome sequencing data in a mutually acceptable electronic format that preserves study participants� confidentiality. Data delivered will include: per sample CRAMs per sample gVCFs per sample VCFs joint-called multi-sample VCF per sample structural variant and CNV calls QC report and data dictionary Sample manifest with flagged problems Following data delivery and upon request by the Government, the contractor shall provide attendance at Government laboratory staff meetings, and the contractor shall provide technical consultations as needed. The contractor will also ship overnight on dry ice any leftover samples on plates to the Biomedical Research Center in Baltimore, MD. Please refer to the attachments for complete details, specifications and relevant information.

We recently made changes to the Challenge Stream; we have outlined the new parameters: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/challenges Steps to apply: Step 1: Read this challenge. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/minerva-initiative-arctic-uncrewed-air-system?auHash=6CHvUJo1TFseah1BoKfUzu0d5rKaz3SNEPiCsitv82I MINERVA Initiative – Arctic Uncrewed Air System The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Army (CA) requires an uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) to conduct intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance in Arctic operational conditions that is domestically produced, easy to operate and maintain, and adequately rugged to enable the Canadian soldier to successfully fight and survive on the future battlefield. Challenge sponsor: Department of National Defense (DND) Funding mechanism: Contract Opening date: August 13, 2026 Closing date: September 24, 2026, 14:00 Eastern time Challenge Problem statement The Canadian Army (CA) soldier is facing an increasingly complex and dangerous battlespace in the future. A major element of the complexity and danger is the extreme cold weather conditions inherent in operations in the Arctic environment as the CA and Canadian Ranger (CR) executes responsibilities for sovereignty operations and Search and Rescue (SAR). The CA presently lacks an UAS capable of conducting intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance in Arctic conditions. The CA requires an innovative uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) that provides an uncrewed alternative to gather information shareable with Other Government Departments (OGD) while operating in extreme cold weather conditions. This innovation must be simple, durable, and highly survivable providing soldiers with an effective capability for future conflicts that integrates seamlessly into operations while minimizing training and maintenance requirements, allowing soldiers to focus on their mission. Desired outcomes and considerations Essential (mandatory) outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Be composed of an: a. Air vehicle: The airframe containing the onboard electronics, propulsion, and payload. b. Sensor payload: The equipment required for navigation and to complete a mission, such as cameras or imaging systems. c. Ground control station: The system (laptop, tablet, or handheld controller) used by the human operator to control flight and manage missions. d. Radio: The wireless system that connects the GCS to the UAS to transmit commands and receive telemetry/data. e. Battery with charger: A battery for the UAS and a battery charger capable of charging multiple batteries simultaneously. f. Remote antenna: An external antenna placed 30m away from the GCS to enhance signal strength, reduce interference, and extend operational range. 2. Operate in various weather conditions. At a minimum: a. Operate in a temperature range of -40°C and +40°C; b. Operate in a minimum windspeed of up to 55 km/hr; c. Operate in light rain or snow ranging from 0.5mm/m²/hr; and d. Operate in moderate icing conditions ranging from 6 g/cm²/hr. 3. Have both a minimum operational radius of 20km and a minimum endurance of 90 min. in continuous movement. 4. Have a sensor that enables the operator to recognize¹ a target at a minimum distance under the following conditions: a. Day: Person (180cm) at 0.5km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x 2m) at 1km b. Night: Person (180cm) at 0.25km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x2m) at 0.5km 5. Be stowable in a 240-litre container. 6. Have a maximum takeoff weight of no more than 25kg. 7. Be capable of operating at a minimum operational altitude of 1000 feet Above Ground Levels (AGL). 8. Allow for operability of the GCS while wearing winter gloves. ¹. “Recognize” is defined by the Johnson Criteria: Detection, Recognition, and Identification (DRI) are all guidelines that have been set in place by The Night Vision Thermal Imaging Systems Performance Model, also referred to as the Johnson criteria (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson%27s_criteria). Additional Outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Be deployable from a stowed state to ready state in 30 minutes or less. This includes completing all tasks (i.e. unloading vehicle, loading/fueling the power system and loading/configuring mission set) such that the vehicle is fully prepped and ready for launch. 2. Be capable of conducting vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) in a maximum area of 2 m². 3. Emit no more than 5 decibels Sound Pressure Level (dB SPL) of noise in all frequency ranges, measured at a 500m distance from the UAS. 4. Be capable of operating with fibre-optic wire, or an alternate non-Electromagnetic (EM) spectrum means. 5. Return to a pre-determined location, hover/loiter, and/or climb in case of loss of link. 6. Have an aggregated projected production cost of $60,000 CAD or less per system. 7. Have a Ground Control Station (GCS) that: a. Incorporates a training simulation capability for Mission Planning. b. Has a minimum remote antenna cable length of 50m. c. Enables UAS navigation via both direct operator control and autonomously using waypoint navigation via the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). d. Displays the following information: i. Location of vehicle in 6 figure Military Grid Reference System (MGRS); ii. Orientation of vehicle (pitch/roll/yaw); iii. Point of aim of camera in 6 figure MGRS; iv. Real-time full motion video feed; v. Altitude in Metres above Sea Level (MSL); and vi. Battery life. e. Can interface with the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK) battle management system to push UAS Position Location Information (PLI) and target PLI. 8. Have an alternate non-electric or hybrid power system that does not rely solely on a battery (i.e. a gas-powered system or a gas/electric hybrid power system). 9. Demonstrate capacity in having its critical components produced and sourced in countries within the NATO alliance, NATO Partners or Major Non-NATO Allies (https://www.nato.int/en/what-we-do/partnerships-and-cooperation/natos-partnerships) . To achieve this, Offerors are requested to provide as an attachment to their proposal, a list identifying the solution's critical components, the country of production and sourcing for each component. title: X-Ray Inspection System
description: Introduction The National Research Council of Canada (NRC) is seeking information regarding advanced X-ray inspection systems to support the research, development, characterization, and failure analysis of rechargeable battery technologies. The NRC's Automotive and Surface Transportation (AST) Research Centre conducts research and testing on a broad range of energy storage systems, including lithium-ion, sodium-ion, solid-state, and emerging battery technologies intended for transportation, aerospace, defence, and stationary energy storage applications. As battery systems become increasingly complex and energy dense, there is a growing need for non-destructive techniques capable of revealing internal structural features and defects that may affect performance, reliability, safety, and manufacturability. X-ray inspection provides a valuable method for visualizing internal battery structures without disassembly, enabling researchers to evaluate cell construction, manufacturing quality, degradation mechanisms, and failure modes throughout the product lifecycle. The AST team operates one of Canada's leading battery testing and characterization facilities, supporting government, industry, and academic partners across the battery value chain. The addition of advanced X-ray inspection capabilities would complement existing electrochemical, thermal, and safety testing infrastructure by providing high-fidelity internal imaging of battery components and assemblies. Objectives The primary objective of this Request for Information (RFI) is to identify and evaluate commercially available X-ray inspection systems suitable for rechargeable battery research, development, characterization, and failure analysis applications. NRC is particularly interested in high-resolution two-dimensional (2D) X-ray imaging systems capable of examining battery cells, cell components, and related assemblies. While inspection throughput is not a primary consideration, image quality, spatial resolution, defect detection capability, sample manipulation flexibility, system versatility, and suitability for laboratory-based research are of significant interest. The information gathered through this RFI will assist NRC in understanding the current state of available technologies, identifying relevant capabilities and limitations, and informing the development of future technical requirements. AMD 001 to answer questions 1 to 4.

Walter Reed National Military Medical Center provides world-class health care to our nation's fighting forces, retirees, and their families. Walter Reed National Military Medical Center, Department of Pathology, Laboratory Services, provides unparalleled pathology expertise to the nation�s military and federal health services, while the centers overall mission is to deliver the highest quality evidence-based laboratory services, foster research, and disseminate new knowledge to advance medical science and military medicine. The department is integral to the National Capital Region�s Academic Health System, with pathologists serving as practitioners in anatomic and clinical pathology at WRNMMC, the Joint Pathology Center (JPC), the National Cancer Institute of the NIH, Fort Belvoir Community Hospital, and other Medical Treatment Facilities across the National Capital Region 4.0 Coordination Requirement: 4.1.1. title: Freedom Connection Natural Gas Pipeline
description: SOURCES SOUGHT - REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FREEDOM CONNECTION NATURAL GAS PIPELINE THIS NOTICE IS FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) OR INVITATION FOR BID. This announcement seeks information from industry which will be used for preliminary planning purposes. This is not a solicitation for proposals, and no contract will be awarded from this synopsis. No solicitation, specifications or drawings are available at this time. 1.0 Introduction and Purpose The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA) is conducting market research for the construction of the Freedom Connection Natural Gas Pipeline in Puerto Rico. The results of this market research will help determine the final procurement strategy. USACE-SAA is issuing this follow up Request for Information due to changes in the design, scope of work and acquisition strategy. This request is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities, and qualifications of Small Business concerns, certified HUBZone, 8(a), Woman-Owned Small Businesses, Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business or Veteran-Owned Small Business. The responses or submissions will be used for informational and planning purposes only and do not constitute a commitment by the Government. The Government will not pay for any information submitted, and respondents will not be notified of the results. Submission or responses to this request for information is not a prerequisite for any potential future offerings. 2.0 Background The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) is funding the Freedom Connection Project. The objective is to enhance the resilience of Puerto Rico�s northern power grid by improving fuel infrastructure. This project involves constructing an approximately 4.2-mile, 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline to supply the Palo Seco Power Plant from the existing San Juan liquid natural gas (LNG) terminal. SAA anticipates soliciting and awarding one (1) design-bid-build solicitation in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Parts 15 and 36. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 237120 - Oil and Gas Pipeline and Related Structures Construction. The small business size standard for this NAICS code is US $45 million. The estimated magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. Anticipated award date is in the second quarter of Fiscal Year 2027. Performance Period is 365 calendar days from NTP. 3.0 Scope of Work The scope of work includes all integrated procurement, labor, equipment, and services required to construct and commission the new pipeline based on a forthcoming final engineering design. Core responsibilities include: � Materials Procurement: Procure all necessary items, including long-lead items such as 20� steel pipe, valves, fittings, and instrumentation, ensuring compliance with the final design and industry standards. � Site Work: Prepare access roads and rights-of-way, and perform site clearing, grading, and stabilization. � Pipeline Installation: Execute all installation activities, including: Trenchless methods (e.g., Horizontal Directional Drilling - HDD). Open trench cut-and-cover installation. Pre-fabrication of materials. Pipeline welding, non-destructive testing (NDT), and inspection. Application of protective external coatings. Above-grade pipeline installation, potentially requiring more than 50 feet deep concrete piles. � Facilities Construction: Build all standalone facilities, including mainline block-valve stations and pig launcher/receiver stations, including electrical and instrumentation. � Delegated Design: Manage and execute any potentially delegated design elements (e.g., temporary works, trench shoring, specialized HDD drill profiles, or structural supports), including coordination with and sealing by licensed Professional Engineers. � Testing and Commissioning: Perform hydrostatic pressure testing, leak detection, and all pre-startup commissioning protocols. � Restoration and Handover: Restore all disturbed areas and formally transfer the completed pipeline and facilities to the owner/operator. 4.0 Requested Information for Capability Statement Interested firms must submit a capability statement (limited to 10 pages) that addresses the following. Responses should be tailored to demonstrate the firm's ability to successfully manage and execute this integrated procurement and construction project. Corporate Information & Experience 1. Company Profile: Provide your firm's name, address, point of contact (POC), CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). 2. Business Category: Specify your firm's socioeconomic status (e.g., Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), HUBZone, 8(a), Woman-Owned Small Business). 3. Bonding Capacity: Include documentation from your bonding company showing current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. 4. Project Experience: Interested construction firms may provide no more than three (3) example projects where the interested firm served as the prime contractor. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages and quality of performance. Example projects must be of similar size and scope. Projects similar in scope to this project include: Natural gas pipeline project of similar magnitude and complexity where your firm was responsible for both materials� procurement and construction. Civil projects involving trenchless technologies like HDD, and work in dense urban or environmentally sensitive areas. Each project must comprise of detailed scope of the work, performance timeline, dollar value, customer name. Construction of pipelines of more than 1 mile in length including trenchless pipeline installation, including horizontal directional drilling, jack and bore, and other trenchless technologies. 5.0 Submission Instructions � Deadline: Responses must be submitted via email no later than 10:00 AM (AST), Tuesday, 24 September 2026. � Email To: Angel.J.Martinez@usace.army.mil and Meranda.R.Booth@usace.army.mil. � Format: No hardcopy or facsimile submissions will be accepted. The capability statement shall be limited to ten (10) pages. Any commercial brochures or currently existing marketing material may also be submitted.

title: Pre-Solicitation Notice of Intent to Sole-Source
description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE TO NEGOTIATE ON A SOLE SOURCE BASIS The Office of Acquisition and Agreements Management (OAAM), Acquisition Management Division (AMD), of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), on behalf of the NIST Material Measurement Laboratory (MML), intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Grenova, Inc. (formerly Peak Analysis and Automation, Inc.), 1900 Ellen Road, Richmond, VA 23230-4213 (UEI: XSCGMEZKBZB9), for the acquisition of a new Living Measurement Systems Foundry (LMSF) automation system and equipment necessary to modernize the existing Government-owned LMSF automation system. NIST requires a complete, integrated laboratory automation solution to expand the capabilities of the existing LMSF. The Contractor shall furnish one new LMSF automation system capable of supporting automated microbial culture, sample preparation, and analytical workflows. The system shall include all required laboratory instrumentation, robotic liquid handling equipment, robotics, automated plate handling and storage equipment, biological containment equipment, computers, software, firmware, licenses, accessories, and other components necessary to provide a complete and fully operational automation system. The Contractor shall also furnish a new Hamilton Company MicroLab STAR liquid handling platform and all associated hardware, software, firmware, licenses, and integration components necessary to modernize the existing Government-owned LMSF. The replacement platform shall be integrated with the remaining Government-owned equipment while preserving the existing system's automation functionality, software operation, laboratory workflows, operating parameters, and measurement methodologies. As part of furnishing the new and modernized LMSF automation systems, the Contractor shall provide all necessary system design, configuration, integration, programming, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), delivery, installation, Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), commissioning, documentation, operator training, and warranty support necessary to provide NIST with complete and operational systems. The anticipated acquisition will be Firm-Fixed-Price and will consist of an eighteen (18)-month base period for delivery, integration, installation, testing, training, and acceptance of the new and modernized LMSF automation systems. The acquisition is also anticipated to include three (3) one-year option periods for maintenance and support following expiration of the applicable warranty periods. Sole source determination is based on the following: NIST's minimum requirement is not simply for commercially available laboratory instrumentation. The Government requires a second LMSF automation system that functions as a measurement-equivalent and interoperable automation platform with the existing LMSF. The new and modernized systems must preserve compatibility with existing laboratory workflows, automation routines, software functionality, operating parameters, and measurement methodologies. Grenova, Inc. (formerly Peak Analysis and Automation, Inc.) designed, integrated, delivered, installed, and commissioned the Government's existing LMSF automation system and has subsequently provided maintenance, technical support, and system upgrades. As the original system integrator, Grenova possesses unique knowledge of the existing LMSF system architecture, hardware and software integration, automation programming, equipment interfaces, control strategies, and operational characteristics. NIST has operated and characterized the existing LMSF for approximately eight years. During this period, NIST has quantified contributions to measurement uncertainty associated with robotic manipulation, liquid transfers, incubation, spectrophotometric measurements, and other automated operations. The Government therefore requires the second system to reproduce the operational characteristics of the existing LMSF sufficiently to permit the two systems to function as interchangeable measurement systems without introducing unacceptable differences in measurement performance. The modernization of the existing LMSF requires replacement of the currently integrated Hamilton MicroLab STAR liquid handling platform while maintaining the functionality of the remaining Government-owned automation system. Successful modernization requires integration of the replacement equipment with existing robotics and instrumentation and migration or preservation of applicable automation software, configuration files, control logic, drivers, communication settings, automation routines, and operational parameters. The original LMSF was acquired under Contract No. SB134118SU0017. The original contract did not include FAR clause 52.227-14 or otherwise establish Government rights to use technical data, including designs developed under the award. Consequently, it is unclear to what extent the Government may use the original system's hardware and software designs, integration information, automation routines, and related technical information to enable another source to reproduce the existing LMSF design. Market research indicates that Grenova is the only known source capable of furnishing the complete requirement, including a functionally equivalent LMSF automation system, the equipment and integration necessary to modernize the existing Government-owned LMSF, and follow-on support for both systems. Acquisition from another source is expected to result in substantial duplication of cost and unacceptable delays associated with redevelopment, integration, testing, requalification, and validation of an alternative system. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 334516 � Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing, with a small business size standard of 1,000 employees. No solicitation package will be issued. This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, responsible sources that believe they can satisfy the Government's requirements may submit a written capability statement demonstrating their ability to furnish the complete requirement. Capability statements shall specifically address the respondent's ability to: Furnish a complete laboratory automation system incorporating robotic liquid handling equipment, laboratory instrumentation, robotics, automated plate handling, automation software, and biological containment equipment; Furnish and integrate equipment manufactured by multiple Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) into a unified laboratory automation system; Furnish a system capable of operating interoperably with the Government's existing LMSF while preserving or reproducing existing automation routines, software functionality, operating parameters, laboratory workflows, and measurement methodologies; Furnish and integrate a replacement Hamilton Company MicroLab STAR liquid handling platform into the existing Government-owned LMSF while preserving the functionality and performance of the remaining system; and Provide the warranty, maintenance, replacement parts, software support, and technical support necessary to sustain both LMSF automation systems. Respondents shall identify any Government-furnished technical data, system design information, software, interface documentation, proprietary information, licenses, or other information that would be required for the respondent to furnish a system satisfying the Government's requirements. Responses must be received by September 24, 2026. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed acquisition based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

description: The Marine Corps Installation, National Capital Region, Regional Contracting Office (MCINCR-RCO), Marine Corps Base Quantico, VA currently has a follow-on requirement for the United States Marine Corps (USMC), Training and Education Command (TECOM) Range Training Area Management (RTAM) Support. The procurement of services in support of TECOM shall be solicited as a competitive Small Business concern. The contemplated contract will be a single award, Firm Fixed Priced contract. The resultant contract will have a 12?month base period followed by four (4) additional 12?month option periods, which may be exercised at the Government�s discretion. The NAICS code associated with this requirement is 541990. This action will be solicited utilizing FAR Part 12 in conjunction with Part 15 Contracting by Negotiation procedures. All terms, conditions, evaluation procedures, and instructions to offerors will be specified in an upcoming Request for Proposals (RFP) that will be posted on this website (SAM.gov). The proposed solicitation number for this action is M00264-26-R-0005. All responsible sources must submit a proposal to be considered for this requirement. All interested parties must be registered in the System Award Management (SAM.gov). It is the responsibility of the interested parties to independently review the referenced web link (SAM.gov) frequently for updates to any and all documents. Potential offerors will be responsible for downloading their copy of the RFP and amendments, if any. SCOPE OF WORK: The Range and Training Area Management Branch, TECOM requires contractor support to provide specialized expertise for the Marine Corps Range Program, including aviation range safety, ground range safety, laser range safety, range certification, Range Facility Management Support System (RFMSS) support, administrative services, range safety training, Range Managers Tool Kit (RMTK) support, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) data maintenance and development, Range Operations Professional Development (ROPD) curriculum development, range training systems, and installation?level range operations support. These services require multi?service experience in classroom instruction, range integration, range certification, and airspace/Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) workflows. This support is essential to the modernization, upgrading, transformation, safety, and sustainment of USMC Operational Training Ranges.

buyer: The Common Services Agency (more commonly known as Public Services Delivery Scotland) (PSD Scotland)
title: Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme
description: NHS Scotland intends to establish a national Framework Agreement for the provision of a Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme. The programme will support individuals identified as being at risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes and/or those diagnosed with primary hypertension, through the delivery of evidence-based, digitally enabled lifestyle and behaviour change interventions. The Authority intends to appoint a single supplier to a national Framework Agreement. The procurement will be conducted using a Restricted Procedure, comprising a Selection Stage and an Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage. Suppliers will be shortlisted following evaluation of their suitability, technical and professional capability, capacity and relevant experience, with a maximum of five suppliers invited to submit a tender.

title: J065--Surgical Table Maintenance - NWI 36C26324P0005 (VA-27-00004588) (Patterson-Elliott)
description: This is a Notice of Intent published in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 5.101(a)(1) requiring the dissemination of information regarding proposed contract actions. This Notice of Intent is for a proposed award of a sole source, firm-fixed price contract under the authority of 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 13.106-1(b) - Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Service Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. It is not a request for competitive quotes. The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 23 intends to award a sole source, firm-fixed price contract to Baxter for maintenance of Trusystem 7000DV surgical table in use by the VA. The required maintenance services are proprietary to Baxter/Hill-ROM in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 13.106-1(b) - Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Service Will Satisfy Agency Requirements because the equipment, software and services are unique or proprietary to Baxter Inc. Market research revealed that Baxter Inc. is the proprietary developer and distributor for the equipment currently being utilized by VA. Additionally, Baxter is the only manufacturer that can provide the required maintenance support for the equipment. The equipment is routinely used by VA to provide medical services for veterans in the VA Healthcare System. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 811210 and the service code is J065. While this synopsis does not constitute a solicitation, interested vendors may identify their interest and capability to satisfy the requirement. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be considered by the agency. The Government understands that Baxter Inc. is the only vendor that can provide the requested services. However, vendors that believe they can provide the capabilities required to fully meet the Government's requirement may submit information in writing to savannah.weberg@va.gov within ten calendar days after publication of this notice. Such documentation will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct the procurement on a competitive basis. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: Sources Sought/Market Intelligence Notice: Selfridge KC-46 Dual Bay Hangar Complex � Use of Construction Management at Risk using Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, has a requirement for the design and construction of Dual Bay (Fuel Cell and General Maintenance) Hangar for the KC-46 Pegasus aircraft at Selfridge ANG, MI. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary equipment, materials, labor, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver a fully functional maintenance hangar including required shops as indicated below: General Purpose Shop Corrosion Control Shop Fuel Cell Shop: Weapons System Maintenance Engine Shop Avionics Shop Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $188,700,000 PLANNED ACQUISITION STRATEGIES UNDER EVALUATION: Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA). The Louisville District is evaluating a Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) strategy utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This authority is intended for military construction projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies to achieve potential benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. Currently, the Government has advanced the design to 35% and has the capability to progress to a full design. Therefore, the Government is utilizing this RFI to assess industry capability, interest, and the advantages of utilizing Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The CM@Risk Course of Action (10 U.S.C. � 2808a): This path allows USACE to execute a construction project where the design is brought at near 65% completion. Phase 1 Preconstruction: The builder is hired during Phase 1 to act as an expert consultant, helping the Designer of Record (DOR) push the design from 65% to 100% using real-time market data and MII (MCACES 2nd Generation) cost comparisons. Phase 2 Construction: Once the design hits 100% and the MII estimate validates the open-book pricing, the agreement transitions to Phase 2, where the builder goes "At-Risk" to construct the facility under a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). The DOR retains design liability, but the contractor drives constructability and assumes responsibility for layout, schedule, and trade coordination. The CM@Risk Pricing Structure: Preconstruction Services Fee: A small, fixed-price or time-and-materials amount paid to the contractor strictly to fund their time spent helping the Architect Engineer (A/E) finalize the 65% design into a 100% design. The Target Fee: The contractor�s transparent profit margin for managing the actual construction, bid competitively upfront. The GMP: The absolute ceiling for the construction phase (Validated Direct Costs + Target Fee + Shared Contingency). PHASED EXECUTION PLAN Phase 1: Preconstruction Services Agreement (CM@Risk Advisory) Solicitation (White Papers): The Solicitation would likely include the 35% design. The Deliverable is anticipated to be a concise 5-10 page White Paper. Evaluation Criteria will likely include Corporate capability and experience with collaborative project delivery methods ( including CM@Risk, Progressive Design-Build (PDB) and/or Design-Build to Budget (DBtB)) under an OT framework; preconstruction approach (how the firm plans to collaborate with the Government's A/E to close the remaining 65% design gap, identify value-engineering opportunities, and mitigate supply-chain risks); proposed Target Fee (for construction) and Preconstruction Services Fee. The Pitch Meeting (Oral Presentations): A 90-minute pitch where the contractor must bring their Project Manager, Site Superintendent, and their Preconstruction Manager. The Government team assesses how well the contractor's team will integrate with the A/E during the critical final design push. The OT is initially awarded and funded only for the Preconstruction Services Fee. Design Finalization (Bridging the 35% Gap): The contractor�s Preconstruction team sits with the Government and the DOR. Because the design is not locked, they can actively change it. They perform value engineering, finalize equipment selections, and ensure the drawings are 100% constructible. Open Book Pricing vs. MII: As the design reaches 100%, the contractor conducts open-book market outreach. The Government and contractor review actual sub-bids together. USACE cost estimators finalize the Independent Government Estimate (IGE) using the MII software to validate costs and establish the GMP base. Phase 2: Construction Execution Agreement (Going "At-Risk") Execution: The Agreements Officer (AO) executes a bilateral modification to the OT Agreement, incorporating the GMP and funding the physical construction. Risk Allocation: Under CM@Risk, the contractor is now "At-Risk." While the DOR retains design liability, the contractor collaborates to identify constructability conflicts during Phase 1. During Phase 2, while the DOR still owns fundamental engineering failures, the contractor loses the ability to claim "defective design" for constructability issues, material delays, or coordination errors, because they were explicitly paid to help finalize those exact decisions using market and MII data during Phase 1. title: Sources Sought/Market Intelligence Notice: Selfridge KC-46 Dual Bay Hangar Complex � Use of Construction Management at Risk using Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, has a requirement for the design and construction of Dual Bay (Fuel Cell and General Maintenance) Hangar for the KC-46 Pegasus aircraft at Selfridge ANG, MI. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary equipment, materials, labor, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver a fully functional maintenance hangar including required shops as indicated below: General Purpose Shop Corrosion Control Shop Fuel Cell Shop: Weapons System Maintenance Engine Shop Avionics Shop Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $188,700,000 PLANNED ACQUISITION STRATEGIES UNDER EVALUATION: Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA). The Louisville District is evaluating a Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) strategy utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This authority is intended for military construction projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies to achieve potential benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. Currently, the Government has advanced the design to 35% and has the capability to progress to a full design. Therefore, the Government is utilizing this RFI to assess industry capability, interest, and the advantages of utilizing Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The CM@Risk Course of Action (10 U.S.C. � 2808a): This path allows USACE to execute a construction project where the design is brought at near 65% completion. Phase 1 Preconstruction: The builder is hired during Phase 1 to act as an expert consultant, helping the Designer of Record (DOR) push the design from 65% to 100% using real-time market data and MII (MCACES 2nd Generation) cost comparisons. Phase 2 Construction: Once the design hits 100% and the MII estimate validates the open-book pricing, the agreement transitions to Phase 2, where the builder goes "At-Risk" to construct the facility under a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). The DOR retains design liability, but the contractor drives constructability and assumes responsibility for layout, schedule, and trade coordination. The CM@Risk Pricing Structure: Preconstruction Services Fee: A small, fixed-price or time-and-materials amount paid to the contractor strictly to fund their time spent helping the Architect Engineer (A/E) finalize the 65% design into a 100% design. The Target Fee: The contractor�s transparent profit margin for managing the actual construction, bid competitively upfront. The GMP: The absolute ceiling for the construction phase (Validated Direct Costs + Target Fee + Shared Contingency). PHASED EXECUTION PLAN Phase 1: Preconstruction Services Agreement (CM@Risk Advisory) Solicitation (White Papers): The Solicitation would likely include the 35% design. The Deliverable is anticipated to be a concise 5-10 page White Paper. Evaluation Criteria will likely include Corporate capability and experience with collaborative project delivery methods ( including CM@Risk, Progressive Design-Build (PDB) and/or Design-Build to Budget (DBtB)) under an OT framework; preconstruction approach (how the firm plans to collaborate with the Government's A/E to close the remaining 65% design gap, identify value-engineering opportunities, and mitigate supply-chain risks); proposed Target Fee (for construction) and Preconstruction Services Fee. The Pitch Meeting (Oral Presentations): A 90-minute pitch where the contractor must bring their Project Manager, Site Superintendent, and their Preconstruction Manager. The Government team assesses how well the contractor's team will integrate with the A/E during the critical final design push. The OT is initially awarded and funded only for the Preconstruction Services Fee. Design Finalization (Bridging the 35% Gap): The contractor�s Preconstruction team sits with the Government and the DOR. Because the design is not locked, they can actively change it. They perform value engineering, finalize equipment selections, and ensure the drawings are 100% constructible. Open Book Pricing vs. MII: As the design reaches 100%, the contractor conducts open-book market outreach. The Government and contractor review actual sub-bids together. USACE cost estimators finalize the Independent Government Estimate (IGE) using the MII software to validate costs and establish the GMP base. Phase 2: Construction Execution Agreement (Going "At-Risk") Execution: The Agreements Officer (AO) executes a bilateral modification to the OT Agreement, incorporating the GMP and funding the physical construction. Risk Allocation: Under CM@Risk, the contractor is now "At-Risk." While the DOR retains design liability, the contractor collaborates to identify constructability conflicts during Phase 1. During Phase 2, while the DOR still owns fundamental engineering failures, the contractor loses the ability to claim "defective design" for constructability issues, material delays, or coordination errors, because they were explicitly paid to help finalize those exact decisions using market and MII data during Phase 1. title: Sea Lice Genotyping
description: The USDA Agricultural Research Service requires DNA extraction from sea lice (Lepeophtheirus salmonis) and single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) genotyping. Lice tissue samples will consist of single pre-adult or adult animals that have been preserved in ethanol. Sea lice DNA genotyping will be completed using AXIOM LSAL200K 96-ARRAY genotyping in the 96-well format (Thermo-Fisher SKU number 550522) on the GeneTitan Instrument or equal. Deliverables will include the genotyping data for all the samples and the raw data files in .cel format (CEL files) and PLINK format (either .ped and .map or .bed, .bim, and .fam). Unused tissue samples and DNA samples will be sent back to the government. Contractor shall provide all services, supplies, equipment and facilities necessary to provide the deliverable specified in accordance with the terms, conditions, and specifications contained in this document.

description: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS – EXECUTIVE SEARCH FIRM      ABOUT FCC    FCC is proud to be 100% invested in Canadian agriculture and food. Our employees are committed to the long-standing success of those who produce and process Canadian food. FCC provides flexible financing and capital solutions, while creating value through data, knowledge, relationships and expertise. FCC offers a complement of financial and non-financial products and services designed to support the complex and evolving needs of the industry. As a commercial Crown corporation, FCC is a stable partner that reinvests profits back into the industry and communities it serves. For more information, visit fcc.ca.    RFP CONTACT    Farid Sokolovic  Procurement Manager  Farm Credit Canada   procurement@fcc.ca    RFP SCOPE    Farm Credit Canada (FCC) is seeking proposals from qualified executive search firms to provide talent acquisition services for a variety of executive roles. The purpose of this Request for Proposals (RFP) is to enter in a contract with highest scoring Proponent that can assist FCC in attracting, assessing, and retaining qualified candidates who meet the experience, education, language, and competency requirements of various executive roles at FCC.     For further details, refer to the RFP and Appendix A (RFP Schedule, Evaluation Process, Scope and Proposal Instructions) documents that are uploaded to MERX.    RFP PARTICULARS    All conditions for Proponent participation are included in the RFP documents.  Duration of Contract:  Three (3) years    RFP SCHEDULE    RFP Release Date:  August 20, 2026  Proponent Questions Accepted Until:  September 10, 2026 at 2:00PM*  FCC Response to Proponent Questions Delivered Before:  September 17, 2026 at 5:00PM*  RFP Closing Date/Time:  September 24, 2026 at 2:00PM*    NOTE: All times are CST – Saskatchewan. The above dates are subject to change at the sole discretion of FCC. Any changes to the RFP Schedule will be communicated to all Proponents via amendment on MERX.     RFP PROCESS CONSIDERATIONS    This opportunity is covered under the provisions of Chapter 5 (Government Procurement) of the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) and Chapter 19 (Government Procurement) of the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA).  FCC is subject to the Official Languages Act (Canada). Proponents may choose to respond to this RFP in their official language of choice (English or French).  This opportunity notice references a non-binding, competitive RFP, and is not a call for tenders. FCC is not obligated to proceed with the Work described in the RFP Scope, and may cancel the RFP at any time. FCC’s procurement process allows for consecutive or concurrent negotiations between FCC and one (1) or multiple Proponents, prior to awarding a Contract.    MERX ELECTRONIC BIDDING SYSTEM    This Request for Proposals (RFP), including any attachments and amendments to such RFP, is available for download by the Proponent on MERX. MERX is a Canadian Public Tenders electronic bidding system accessible at https://www.merx.com. It is the sole responsibility of the Proponent to ensure its compatibility with MERX.  Proponent proposals MUST be submitted electronically through MERX, preferably in a PDF or MS Word file, prior to the RFP Closing Date/Time specified in the RFP. Proposals submitted in other formats, by other methods or through any other means, or after the RFP Closing Date/Time specified in the RFP, may be rejected by FCC.      PRIORITY OF DOCUMENTS    In the event there are any discrepancies between this opportunity notice and the information on the MERX website proper, this opportunity notice shall take precedence. Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Cheshire and Warrington Outline Water Plan
description: The newly established Cheshire and Warrington Combined Authority (CWCA) has recently stated its intention to commission an Independent Economic Review (IER) for the subregion - setting out the evidence for the opportunities for and constraints on local growth. In support of this, it is vital to better understand where water infrastructure may require upgrades to support local ambition, and how we can better work together to ensure that flooding and drought are not impediments to growth whilst ensuring that wider ecosystem services and farming resilience are better supported. Simultaneously, the Water White Paper published in January 2026 committed Government to act on the Independent Water Commission recommendation, setting up Regional Systems Planning in England. DEFRA have set out an intention to pilot this through Regional System Planners (RSPs), established across each region of England with the aim of influencing both PR29 and other water system investment plans. Defra are keen for partnerships to pilot RSP governance and structures during this set-up year. and have set out that they only intend to provide high level direction on form. Within this context there is a significant opportunity to influence water planning, and ensure alignment with local growth and wider environmental ambitions. To support the IER along with engagement with the establishing North West RSP, ECW is seeking to appoint consultants to develop a strategic, place based evidence base and outline water plan that sits between national/regional water planning processes and local spatial, economic, and infrastructure planning.

description: Notice of Intent to Award to a Single Source - University of Illinois School of Chemical Sciences K101 and K110 pellets This is a Notice of Intent (NOI), not a request for proposal. Mathews, Urbana, IL 61801, USA for a requirement of the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD).
